title: When Not to Imitate: Boundary-Aware Skill Memory for Reliable Tool-Use LLM Agents

visual_explainer.blocker: No paper-grounded mechanism figure was available; the record remains text-only rather than publishing an unverified synthesis.

analysis.tldr: Applicability, risk, avoidance, and recovery fields can suppress imitation traps after skill retrieval; matched attention controls support boundary text, but the package is not Pareto-improving and full lifecycle cost is absent.
analysis.problem: A success-derived procedure can be relevant yet invalid when the current state requires different tools.
analysis.core_idea: Write explicit validity boundaries with each procedure, retrieve under a fixed budget, then apply, suppress, or repair at runtime.

memory_design.write: Successful, failed, and partial trajectories become seven-field skills.
memory_design.organize: A deterministic validator retries or discards malformed skills.
memory_design.read: Semantic/tool retrieval exposes boundary fields under a token budget; a checker gates application and may inject repair guidance.
memory_design.update_forget: No dynamic boundary update, forgetting, or long-horizon library maintenance is evaluated.

compared_to: Procedure Skill from successful trajectories with the same backbone and retrieval
Equal-token procedure padding and same-prompt attention knockouts
analysis.evidence: For Qwen3-8B, Base/Procedure/BASM score 34.13/33.88/38.88 on BFCL and 29.76/33.33/36.31 on AppWorld; AgentDojo ASR falls to 5.90, but utility 35.93 remains below Base 40.99. Boundary knockout recovers 69.4% of the wrong-tool gap.
analysis.why_it_matters: Procedural memory needs an explicit validity contract after retrieval; topical relevance is not authorization to imitate.
limitations: Representation, failed-trajectory admission, retrieval, formatting, checker, and repair all change together.
Prompt-only BASM and repair-only variants hurt AppWorld; several larger-model gains are small and slices reverse.
Extraction, validation, embedding, checker, repair, latency, dollars, GPU-hours, and energy are unreported.
